does: Pulls cooked, tender meat apart along its grain into rough strands, with forks or with the fingers, so that it mixes evenly into a filling or a sauce.

intro.what: Cooked meat is pulled apart along its grain into strands.
intro.why: Strands mix through a filling and hold its sauce better than neat cubes.

how: Let the cooked meat cool until it can be handled.
Take off and throw away any skin, bone and gristle.
Hold a piece with a fork and pull it apart along its grain with a second fork, or tear it with your fingers, into bite-sized strands.

cues.text: The meat comes apart easily along its grain.
Long, rough strands with no skin or bone among them.

mistakes.mistake: Shredding it while it is too hot, which burns the fingers and turns the meat to mush.
mistakes.fix: Let it cool a little first.

mistakes.mistake: Tearing across the grain, which gives short, dry crumbs.

quiz.question: Which way do you pull the meat?
quiz.because: The meat parts easily along its grain into strands.

quiz.question: When is the meat ready to shred?
choices: When it is cooked, tender and cool enough to handle.
